item.text: {"stage":"correction","question_id":"1B.7","answer":null,"critique":null,"corrected":{"question_id":"1B.7","answer":"The reopened evidence does not establish that López Obrador personally appointed qualified independent catastrophic-risk experts, protected their dissent, or replaced expertise with loyalty. It does show substantial expert-oriented nuclear-safety machinery operating under CNSNS and CFE: qualified personnel and external consultants, conflict-of-interest safeguards for consultants, technical decision authority, safety-culture ambassadors, self-assessments, surveys, peer reviews, root-cause analysis, corrective-action systems, emergency training, and regulatory review of staff qualification and requalification (BATCH-0002-E006; BATCH-0002-E007; BATCH-0002-E008; BATCH-0002-E009; BATCH-0002-E010; BATCH-0002-E012). Federal funding supported Laguna Verde operations, training, recruitment, retraining, waste management, and decommissioning provisions; the evidence specifically reports 1,400 permanent employees in CFE’s Nuclear Corporate Coordination and formal qualification systems, but does not show that López Obrador personally made these staffing or resource decisions (BATCH-0002-E008). Mexico also publicly supported IAEA safeguards, transparent peer review, and nuclear-safety cooperation, while its 2023 GMO biosafety committee and 2023 statements on scientific analysis and biological-material controls provide formal expert-oriented commitments rather than proof of appointment independence or implementation (BATCH-0031-E001; BATCH-0031-E002; BATCH-0039-E002; BATCH-0043-E004). The institutional record is materially qualified. CNSNS was subordinate to SENER and lacked full de jure independence; proposals for greater independence had not progressed, the statutory Advisory Council had not been created, and prior reviews identified needs for stronger public communication, inspection, training, and financial resources. The report also states that federal savings policies limited the CNSNS budget (BATCH-0002-E002; BATCH-0002-E003; BATCH-0002-E006). Operational processes supplied meaningful expert access and correction channels, but they were not complete: no dedicated human-and-organizational-factors inspections occurred at Laguna Verde during 2019–2021; a 2019 emergency exercise generated 78 findings and its follow-up was rescheduled; and FLEX Phase 3 and some regulatory conclusion reporting remained unfinished or pending (BATCH-0002-E009; BATCH-0002-E010; BATCH-0002-E011). The 2023 CIDE record shows that external research-fund administration became impossible after institutional changes since 2021 and that a poverty-research data-collection program was suspended indefinitely, but it does not identify the responsible decision-makers or establish ideological suppression (BATCH-0019-E006). Evidence about the broader information environment raises a separate concern about protection of dissent and independent scrutiny: Freedom House reported weakened independent regulators, an INAI quorum crisis, support from López Obrador and allies for dissolving INAI, and probable military-linked surveillance; ARTICLE 19 reported named Pegasus-surveillance cases, presidential denial, an official campaign contesting the reporting, and unresolved accountability. These reports are relevant to the conditions for dissent and oversight, but do not prove that the ruler selected unqualified loyalists in catastrophic-risk institutions or personally directed every military or regulatory action (BATCH-0026-E013; BATCH-0026-E020; BATCH-0018-E003; BATCH-0018-E013). Cybersecurity failures are retained only as limited contextual evidence: the Sedena breach and reported staffing or equipment weaknesses concern institutional risk and corrective capacity, but the reopened passages do not establish a 1B.7 expert-governance failure or personal presidential responsibility (BATCH-0047-E010; BATCH-0008-E006; BATCH-0011-E005). Overall, the best-supported correction is a mixed institutional account: Mexico maintained substantial technical expertise, training, review, and safety-resourcing mechanisms, while formal independence, independent oversight, research continuity, and protection of critical scrutiny remained incomplete or contested. Direct ruler-level evidence remains
